6.name: John Eaves - Star Trek concept illustrator, designer and model maker
6.overview: Bryan & Lili return for the season 6 premiere of their Star Trek talk show with production artist John Eaves. Eaves began with Greg  Jein making models on Star Trek 5:The Final Frontier, with some in-between model work on Star Trek: The Next Generation. Later, after Herman Zimmerman discovered John Eaves did illustrations and drawings at a very high level, he asked him to be on Star Trek: Generations, the 1994 film where Eaves worked with Michael Okuda and others on the Enterprise-B sketch concept design.  Eaves also talks about how Zimmerman asked him to come on board to Star Trek Deep Space Nine soon there after. Part 1 of a 2 part interview.

6.name: John Eaves - Star Trek concept illustrator, designer and model maker, Part 2
6.overview: Our Sagacious hosts, Lili Fox Lim and Bryan Kreutz, continue their incredible interview with special guest John Eaves. In this conversation, we hear from Star Trek's longest-running staff member and his great stories working on concept art, illustrations, and model making. John talks in depth about working on Star Trek Projects from 1989 through 2022. We hear how he got his start working on Deep Space Nine as a production illustrator and how he incorporated his love of making models into that role. Bryan and Lili ask interesting questions about what it was like working with JJ Abrams, as well as working for Paramount on so many Star Trek TV Series. We find out his influences when designing iconic props like the Phaser weapons in Star Trek: Enterprise. John also gives Bryan and Lili insight into what it was like working in a production role that has had so many technological improvements over the years.

6.name: Jonathan Del Arco; My immigration story in a new book, plus Star Trek's Hugh and Fantome
6.overview: Our hosts, Bryan Kreutz and Lili Fox-Lim, beam up special guest Jonathan Del Arco to discuss his newest book, "Freddy the Alien," as well as his roles as Hugh and Fantome. Del Arco brings along his co-author, Trisha DeFazio, and Illustrator Adria Alvarado to discuss the collaboration that went into getting their book published. The trio also discusses the importance of releasing a story like "Freddy the Alien" in today's world. Jonathan also dives into his role at Ricky Diaz on Miami Vice and what it was like working with NBC. They wrap up part one of this exciting interview, talking about the audition process at Paramount for Star Trek.

6.name: Jonathan Del Arco; My immigration story in a new book, plus Star Trek's Hugh and Fantome, Part 2
6.overview: Lili and Bryan continue their thrilling interview with Actor and Author Jonathan Del Arco. But first, Lili tests her knowledge on a challenging segment of Tractor Beam, me. Our magnetic hosts discuss Jonathan's role as the first Borg in Star Trek when he appeared in Star Trek: The Next Generation. He talks about his initial thoughts while reviewing the script. As the questions keep rolling, we find intriguing insight into what it was like on set while shooting for Star Trek: Picard. Lili wraps up the interview, asking Jonathan about his Star Trek: Voyager character Fantone in the season 7 episode "The Void".

overview: A Journalistic news source and interview TV Talk show beaming down the latest Star Trek news and views from all the ships crews. A Captain's Log guides viewers through this side of our galaxy's quadrant with a splash of knowledge in our top 10 lists and interviews. Looking through Roddenberry's Star Trek universe and beyond in this half hour scoop at warp power, host Bryan Kreutz, his co-host Lili Fox-Lim steer viewers into a knowledge-based trek of Klingon language all the way through full interviews with guests the fans want to hear from. Bryan and Lili are accompanied by an animated alter ego named Rogg to humor viewers with relevant Star Trek news and views. From a Starfleet ambassador's point of view, as Ambassador to the fan's, Bryan Kreutz hands over the conn to his animated android counterpart's perspective ranging from logical knowledge to unknowns in Star Trek's Past, present, and beyond.

seasons.name: Season 1
seasons.overview: Season one consisted of 13 television episodes and aired from Jun 30, 2021 through Sep 22, 2021

seasons.name: Season 2
seasons.overview: Season two consisted of 11 television episodes (12) when the finale was later split into two episodes and aired from Mar 1, 2022 through May 17, 2022. Bryan, Lili, and Rogg returned for a second season of talk show news and interviews. Highlights were interviews with stunt performers, actors and a top ten list on best Borg episodes.

seasons.name: Season 3
seasons.overview: Season three consisted of 24 television episodes and aired from Mar 8, 2023 through Aug 27, 2023. The biggest season of episode guests with star power and stunt-power with 24 episodes. Interviews with Star Trek Original Series (1960's) guests to Star Trek: The Next Generation guests, Deep Space Nine, Star Trek: Discovery, Strange New Worlds and more top 10 lists.

seasons.name: Season 4
seasons.overview: The longest season to-date consisting of 32 episodes. Two-part episodes galore to extend the interviews of Star Trek's finest cast/crew.

seasons.name: Season 5
seasons.overview: Season five consists of twenty six episodes beginning with the season premiere interview of Nana Visitor of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine. This season had the very first in-studio guest interview with Tom Morga, Chris Doyle, and J. Suzanne Rampe from Star Trek TNG, DS9, and Voyager join hosts Bryan and Lili. Typically all interviews are recorded remotely and displayed on viewscreen.

seasons.name: Season 6
seasons.overview: Season six consists of thirty-six episodes beginning with the season premiere interview of John Eaves, designer and illustrator best known for his work on the Star Trek franchise. This season is the longest with the most episodes produced in one year to-date. Notable guests include Robin Curtis, Todd Stashwick, Michael Okuda, and many more.
